articles.title: Football Daily - Lloyd's off to the Superclásico & are Spurs finally good again? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Rick & Lloyd are joined by Julien Laurens to discuss De Zerbi’s quiet transformation.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 29 Oct 2026 , · 47 mins

Rick & Lloyd are joined by Julien Laurens to discuss how Roberto De Zerbi is slowly moulding Spurs into his image – and after a blockbuster summer, Julien explains why he is undoubtedly the league’s most powerful manager. How far will this transformation go? Whisper it: could Spurs be last season’s Manchester United? Elsewhere, Rick takes up the mantle from the Monday Night Club and finds out which player has scored the most ‘luxury’ goals this season and Lloyd is off to see Boca Juniors vs River Plate this weekend – otherwise known as the Superclásico, one of football’s fiercest rivalries. Oracle of South American football Tim Vickery tells him how to survive it. Or not. Get in touch with us via WhatsApp on 08000 289 369. articles.title: Euro Leagues - Was Raya robbed & how did Europe react to Kane's Ballon d'Or win? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Was David Raya robbed at the Ballon d'Or? And what did the continent make of Kane's win?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 29 Oct 2026 , · 51 mins

How did Athletic Bilbao's Unai Simon beat David Raya for the Yashin Trophy at the Ballon d'Or? Should the World Cup take priority, or was Raya robbed of the award after a spectacular season at Arsenal? And what has the continent made of Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win? Are the Spanish annoyed that it didn't go to Lamine Yamal, and how has Bayern Munich reacted? Maz Farookhi, Guillem Balague and Julien Laurens discuss it all alongside German football expert Rafa Honigstein. Then, the team reflect on Real Madrid's El Clasico victory, James Horncastle joins the pod to look ahead to the Milan Derby, and why has Kylian Mbappe had to apologise to China? Finally, we discuss Dirk Kuyt's Liverpool reunion as new interim head coach of Fenerbahce. articles.title: Jack Grealish dropped by Everton after breaching club discipline ahead of Newcastle Carabao Cup tie
articles.summary: Jack Grealish was dropped by Everton boss David Moyes for their game against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup fourth round; Everton said the midfielder was 'unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline'
articles.body:
Grealish, who is on loan from Manchester City, missed Saturday's defeat at Arsenal due to illness but had started Everton's previous three Premier League matches against Ipswich, Hull City and Chelsea.

He was dropped by manager David Moyes for their cup tie at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night after reportedly missing a training session.

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie said: "My understanding is the reason he's not involved, and the reason he has been disciplined, is because he failed to show for a training session in the build-up to tonight's cup tie."

Everton vs Newcastle is live on Sky Sports+ .

Jarrad Branthwaite also remained unavailable for a second successive game as he continues to follow concussion protocols.

articles.title: El infierno azul de 'Messinho', la estrella 'olvidada' por Xabi Alonso que quiso jugar en el Madrid
articles.standfirst: Estevao, la joya del fútbol brasileño de 19 años, no logra entrar en los planes de Xabi Alonso en el Chelsea
articles.summary: Estevao, la joya del fútbol brasileño de 19 años, no logra entrar en los planes de Xabi Alonso en el Chelsea
articles.body: Estevao, la joya de 19 años por la que el Chelsea pagó 67 millones fijos al Palmeiras en 2024 y que se incorporó a los 'Blues' en 2025, no vive sus mejores tiempos en Stamford Bridge. El joven brasileño, la promesa que el Real Madrid admiró y no supo encajar, se convirtió en el jugador de moda de la Premier tras marcar el gol de la victoria ante el Liverpool el 5 de octubre de 2025. Un año después Estevao, conocido como 'Messinho' por su talento y habilidad, apenas entra en los planes de Xabi Alonso en el Chelsea. Esta temporada las estadísticas de Estevao con el Chelsea son de 172 minutos en 8 partidos (6 de Premier League y 2 de EFL Cup). El buen rendimiento de Pedro Neto es uno de los principales problemas de Estevao, el 'Messinho' del Chelsea. La BBC destacó que Xabi Alonso no contase con Estevao, que estuvo calentando en la banda, en el partido en el que el Chelsea fue eliminado de la Carabao Cup por el Liverpool. El técnico español apostó antes por Emmanuel Emegha, que o había disputado ni un minuto desde su llegada este verano procedente del Estrasburgo, que por Estevao. "No entiendo cómo Estevao no ha llegado a pisar el terreno de juego esta noche. Debe de estar pensando: '¿Qué más tengo que hacer? Tenemos a dos de nuestras estrellas en ataque lesionadas y, aun así, sigo sin saltar al terreno de juego'", señaló Clinton Morrison, exdelantero del Crystal Palace. Xabi Alonso defendió su decisión de no alinear a Estevao, sugiriendo que el delantero aún se está adaptando a las exigencias físicas del fútbol inglés. "Empezamos con Pedro (Neto), Morgan (Rogers) y Danny Welbeck, y el partido tuvo momentos de gran intensidad. Sabíamos que iba a ser un encuentro físico; además, Malo (Gusto) sufrió calambres, lo que nos obligó a realizar ciertos cambios. La temporada va a ser muy larga y habrá oportunidades para todos", argumentó. Al ser cuestionado directamente sobre Estevao el técnico español apuntó que "podría estar más contento; él quiere jugar. Estoy seguro de que tendrá su momento; es mi responsabilidad». "Sabemos que el fútbol en Inglaterra es muy intenso y hay que estar preparado para ello. Estevao está en su segunda temporada. La temporada va a ser larga", explicó

articles.title: La serie de catastróficas desdichas del Bayern: "Nunca había visto nada igual"
articles.standfirst: Max Eberl comentó que "No creo que muchos clubes hayan tenido que lidiar con esto. Y no hablamos de asuntos triviales"
articles.summary: Max Eberl comentó que "No creo que muchos clubes hayan tenido que lidiar con esto. Y no hablamos de asuntos triviales"
articles.body: El Bayern de Múnich está atravesando unos tiempos convulsos fuera del césped que podrían afectar a su rendimiento a la hora de afrontar el exigente calendario que les espera. El trágico fallecimiento del padre de Joshua Kimmich, el susto por la salud de Vincent Kompany y las lesiones Jamal Musiala, Manuel Neuer y Luis Díaz preocupan en las oficinas de un Bayern que mira con preocupación su inminente calendario. El clásico ante el Borussia Dortmund y el viaje a Madrid para enfrentarse al Atlético en Champions League son sus siguientes compromisos. Bastian Schweinsteiger, jugador del Bayern del 2002 al 2015, reconoció en ARD que "bueno, lo pensé mucho antes, ¿ha ocurrido algo así antes en el Bayern de Múnich? Hay tantas situaciones. Claro, con Harry Kane (por el Balón de Oro), por supuesto, eso es lo positivo, pero si piensas en Vincent Kompany, que un entrenador sea sustituido de esa manera... Nunca han habido nada parecido en el Bayern, hay tantos temas que tratar". Max Eberl, director deportivo del Bayern, coincidió con Schweinsteiger sobre la serie de catastróficas desdichas que está sufriendo el equipo alemán. "No creo que muchos clubes hayan tenido que lidiar con esto. Y no hablamos de asuntos triviales. (...) Son cuestiones muy alejadas del fútbol, que nos demuestran que el fútbol no es lo más importante, sino que desempeña un papel secundario. Pero son cuestiones en las que, como seres humanos, tenemos que ocuparnos de otros asuntos. Y eso es lo que estamos haciendo ahora mismo en el Bayern. Por eso es un momento difícil, y se puede ver cómo el club se está uniendo", destacó.

articles.title: Marcos Senna ya tiene “su” campo de fútbol en Brasil
articles.standfirst: El Villarreal aporta 415.000 euros para construir un nuevo campo en la Academia Pelé, institución que colabora con el Villarreal en Resende
articles.summary: El Villarreal aporta 415.000 euros para construir un nuevo campo en la Academia Pelé, institución que colabora con el Villarreal en Resende
articles.body: La leyenda del Villarreal, Marcos Senna, ya tiene un campo de fútbol con su nombre en Brasil. El campeón de la Eurocopa 2008 con España fue homenajeado este miércoles en Resende, al sur de Río de Janeiro, durante la inauguración de una nueva instalación de césped sintético en la Academia Pelé, colaboradora directa del Villarreal en el país sudamericano. El proyecto ha sido posible gracias a la aportación de 415.000 euros del Villarreal, donde el brasileño actualmente ejerce como embajador y director de Relaciones Institucionales: “A nivel personal, es un sueño. Jamás imaginé que inauguraría un campo con mi nombre. Pero lo más importante es para las generaciones venideras”, reconoció el ex futbolista durante el acto. Senna destacó también el impacto que tendrá la instalación para los jóvenes de la región: «Esta nueva instalación permitirá más horas de entrenamiento para muchas categorías. Dado el talento que tenemos aquí, estoy seguro de que será muy importante para la Academia Pelé y para toda la región». La iniciativa se enmarca en el acuerdo de colaboración que el Villarreal mantiene con el Resende y la Academia Pelé desde septiembre de 2024. La alianza contempla el intercambio de metodologías de entrenamiento y el desarrollo de jóvenes talentos brasileños, con la posibilidad de que algunos sean evaluados por el club amarillo. De hecho, nueve futbolistas de la cantera ya han viajado a España para conocer de primera mano la metodología del Submarino. Con este nuevo campo, el Villarreal refuerza su apuesta por la formación y la proyección internacional de jóvenes promesas en una de las más de 30 academias asociadas que el Villarreal tiene en más de 20 países diferentes

articles.title: Danilo renueva con Flamengo: "Es el equipo que llevo en el corazón desde que era niño"
articles.standfirst: El internacional brasileño, de 35 años, amplía su contrato hasta 2027
articles.summary: El internacional brasileño, de 35 años, amplía su contrato hasta 2027
articles.body: La aventura de Danilo en el Flamengo continuará un año más. El defensa brasileño ha llegado a un acuerdo con el club de Río de Janeiro y acaba de renovar su contrato por una temporada más. Fichado de la Juventus en enero de 2025, Danilo conquistó la pasada temporada el Brasileirao y la Copa Libertadores, competición en la que fue protagonista al marcar el gol de la victoria en la final contra el Palmeiras. "El Flamengo es el equipo que llevo en el corazón desde que era niño, y no sólo yo, sino también toda mi familia. Por eso tiene todo el sentido continuar un año más con este bonito proyecto que estamos construyendo. Desde que llegué aquí, después de pasar por un período normal de adaptación, me he sentido muy bien en la ciudad, en el club y en el centro de entrenamiento, trabajando junto a todas las personas que viven el Flamengo las 24 horas del día", aseguró Danilo. "Tuvimos una primera temporada muy exitosa, en la que conquistamos varios trofeos, especialmente la Copa Libertadores y el Campeonato Brasileño. Este año estamos luchando por el título de la liga brasileña y queremos afrontar las próximas temporadas con mucha ambición, porque este club siempre aspira a lo máximo y siempre quiere luchar por más. Miro al futuro con mucho entusiasmo y seguiré ayudando al Flamengo, dentro y fuera del campo, a alcanzar sus objetivos. Una vez Flamengo, siempre Flamengo", insistió el ex de Santos, Oporto, Real Madrid, Manchester City y Juventus. Danilo ha disputado 57 partidos con la camiseta rojinegra del Flamengo, en los que ha marcado 6 goles y repartido dos asistencias. Hasta la fecha, el internacional brasileño, de 35 años, ha conquistado un título del Campeonato Brasileño, una Copa Libertadores, dos Campeonatos Cariocas y una Supercopa de Brasil. Gracias al triunfo en la Copa Libertadores, también participó en la Copa Intercontinental, alcanzando la final, que posteriormente perdió contra el PSG en la tanda de penaltis. Con el 'Mengão' también participó en el Mundial de Clubes, donde logró marcar en el partido contra el Chelsea, equipo que acabaría conquistando el torneo. Además, gracias a la conquista de la Copa Libertadores, Danilo se convirtió en el primer jugador de la historia en ganar dos veces tanto la UEFA Champions League como la Copa Libertadores, y en el tercer jugador en marcar con la camiseta del Flamengo en una final de la Libertadores.

El equipo dirigido por Mila Martínez consiguió tres victorias en sus tres primeros encuentros del campeonato y avanzó a octavos con pleno de puntos. España comenzó su participación imponiéndose por 2-0 a México, posteriormente venció por 3-1 a Australia y cerró la fase de grupos con otro triunfo por 3-1 ante Chile. En ese último encuentro, María Aymerich abrió el marcador y Quintana firmó un doblete para asegurar la tercera victoria española antes del comienzo de las eliminatorias. El encuentro ante Estados Unidos supone ahora el primer partido a vida o muerte para la selección española. Ya no hay margen para el error: el ganador continuará adelante en el campeonato y conseguirá una plaza entre las ocho mejores selecciones del torneo. articles.title: Indian Football League: Nagaland United open new chapter for football in the state
articles.summary: Nagaland United Sports Club will begin a new chapter in Indian football when they take on Real Kashmir in the opening match of the 2026-27 Indian Football
articles.body: Nagaland United Sports Club will begin a new chapter in Indian football when they take on Real Kashmir in the opening match of the 2026-27 Indian Football League (IFL) season on October 30. The match will be played at the TRC Stadium in Srinagar.The club will become the first team from Nagaland to compete in the national league. Founded in 2024 in Chümoukedima, Nagaland United have reached this level in just two years, giving a state with a rich football history its long-awaited place in the competition.The club’s journey is also linked to Dr. Talimeren Ao, who captained independent India’s football team at the 1948 Olympic Games. Nearly eight decades after Ao led the country at the Olympics, Nagaland United will carry the state’s football hopes onto the national stage.From first match to national league in two yearsNagaland United played their first competitive match on January 28, 2025, against Barak FC. The game was the opening fixture at a newly opened stadium in Chümoukedima. The date was special because it would have been Ao’s 107th birthday.The team lost the match 2-3 but soon made their presence felt in the Nagaland Super League. They finished second among seven teams in the league phase, conceding only nine goals in 12 matches, and ended the season in third place overall.Forward Nisede Peseyie scored a hat-trick against 27 United and won one of the league’s individual awards. Head coach Khogen Singh was named coach of the season.Nagaland United added their first major trophy in October 2025 when they won the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy in Kohima. They recorded wins by 7-0, 2-1 and 4-0 in the knockout rounds before beating Chedema Village Youth Organisation 3-1 in the final on October 18.Arap Konyak, Joel Haokip and Manton Konyak scored in the final. The club also won the player of the tournament, best goalkeeper and best defender awards, while Singh was once again named the best coach.Talimeren Ao: The man who put Indian football on the Olympic stageThe story of football in Nagaland goes back to Ao, whose early days in the game were far removed from the modern facilities available to players today.He began playing football on the mission playground at Impur in the Naga Hills. Children played barefoot, using balls made from rags, woven cane or even pomelos.Ao’s father, the first Reverend in the Naga Hills, died of typhoid before his son reached his late teens. He had wanted Ao to become a doctor and serve the Naga people.Ao fulfilled that wish by practising medicine, but he also went on to make history in football.On July 31, 1948, he captained India in the country’s first Olympic football match as an independent nation. India faced France at Cricklefield Stadium in Ilford, east London, and lost 1-2 after conceding a goal in the final minute. Eight Indian players played without boots.When asked about playing barefoot, Ao famously replied: “We play football in India, whereas you play bootball.”After returning to India, Ao continued his medical career and became Nagaland’s first Director of Health Services. His legacy remains important in a state where football is closely connected to community life.“Football in Nagaland is more than just a sport,” says coach Kivilu Kiba.‘We do not have the time’Despite the state's love for football, no club from Nagaland had played in the national league before Nagaland United's entry. The club's leadership felt that waiting to move up through the lower divisions would take too long.“It would have taken us years,” says Abu Metha, a member of the club’s board, “and we do not have the time.”Nagaland United secured their place in the IFL through a goodwill agreement with Aizawl FC of Mizoram. Aizawl had made history in 2017 by becoming the first team from the Northeast to win the national league. They secured the title after drawing 1-1 with Shillong Lajong on the final day of the season.William Koso, the first coach from Nagaland to earn an AFC ‘A’ licence, was part of Aizawl’s coaching staff during that historic campaign.The connection between the clubs grew stronger in June 2026, when Aizawl visited Nagaland for a match under the Football for Peace initiative. The fixture, held in Chümoukedima on June 6, was called “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”. Tickets cost Rs 20, and the proceeds went to an orphanage. Aizawl won the match 2-0.Aizawl owner Robert R. Royte later backed Nagaland’s efforts to gain representation in the national league.On September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement that allowed Nagaland United to take Aizawl’s place in the IFL. Aizawl also agreed to provide technical and development support to the Nagaland club.Aizawl had spent 11 consecutive seasons in the national league without relegation. The club will now continue to play in the Mizoram Premier League.The fixture schedule has added another link between the two teams. Nagaland United will travel to Shillong on November 25, the city where Aizawl won their historic title, before visiting Aizawl on December 7.Local players remain a priorityWith their first IFL season approaching, Nagaland United have been working to build a team and support staff capable of handling the demands of national-level football.The club advertised for coaches and support staff and received hundreds of applications. Candidates applied from countries including Argentina, Spain and Brazil.Although Nagaland United have inherited a squad and staff with experience of the national league, developing local footballers remains a key goal.This was highlighted on October 17, when 20-year-old central midfielder Ghuqhe Chishi and Vinato Achumi were recognised after being selected to represent the club in the IFL. Both players have come through Nagaland’s under-20 teams.The club now faces a demanding season. Coordinator Gentleson Vashum said the team would play 20 league matches, with 10 at home and 10 away.Plans are also in place to install FIFA-approved artificial turf at Chümoukedima, which would help the club prepare for the demands of the competition.Nagaland United want to become a symbol of the state across India and beyond. More importantly, they hope their presence in the IFL will give local footballers a clearer path to the national level.“Whenever you enter any arena,” Metha says, “you enter to win.”K. Neibou Sekhose, president of the Nagaland Football Association, has called the club’s entry into the IFL a historic moment. He has also stressed that this is only the beginning of the state’s ambitions in football.Bringing national-league football homeNagaland United will play their first home match in the IFL against Gokulam Kerala on November 14 in Chümoukedima. It is the same venue where they played their first competitive match in January 2025.Dempo are scheduled to visit later in November, while Mohammedan Sporting will arrive on December 19.The 2026-27 IFL season will return to a full home-and-away format, giving Nagaland United the chance to bring national-league football to their home state throughout the campaign.The league has also reported a sharp increase in television viewership, with last season’s audience four times that of the previous season.Nagaland United have appealed to Naga communities living across India, particularly students, to support the team during away matches. Their opening game in Srinagar will be the first opportunity for supporters living far from home to get behind the club.A new chapter in Nagaland footballNagaland United’s rise from a club founded in 2024 to a place in the national league has been quick. But their debut means more than simply competing for points and victories.For a state that produced India’s first Olympic football captain, the club offers a long-awaited chance to turn its passion for the game into a lasting presence in Indian football.When the IFL season begins on October 30, Nagaland United will take the field for their first national-league campaign. They will also carry forward the legacy of Talimeren Ao and aim to create new opportunities for the next generation of footballers from the Naga Hills.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rodri, capitán sin brazalete
articles.standfirst: El medio, aunque acaba de llegar, tiene un peso enorme dentro del vestuario
articles.summary: El medio, aunque acaba de llegar, tiene un peso enorme dentro del vestuario
articles.body: La pasada temporada, Hansi Flick reconoció públicamente que el Barcelona necesitaba líderes capaces de dar un paso al frente en los momentos de dificultad. Este curso, Raphinha ha asumido buena parte de esa responsabilidad y también luce el brazalete de capitán. Sin embargo, hay otro futbolista que, sin llevar la cinta, está ejerciendo como una de las voces de referencia del vestuario azulgrana: Rodri. Pese a que el centrocampista madrileño llegó el pasado mercado de verano, su adaptación al club ha sido rápida y su influencia no ha tardado en hacerse notar. Desde su primera aparición ante la afición, el futbolista ha recibido muestras de cariño de la grada, mientras que dentro del vestuario se ha ganado un peso importante gracias a su personalidad y experiencia. El último ejemplo se produjo ayer miércoles. Después de los dos últimos tropiezos, contra Real Madrid y PSG, Rodri tomó la iniciativa, junto a Raphinha y al resto de los capitanes, para organizar una comida de hermandad de la plantilla. El objetivo era reforzar la unión del grupo. Un gesto que refleja cómo el mediocentro está adquiriendo un papel protagonista. Durante el pasado verano, parecía que el Barcelona tenía bien cubierta la posición de mediocentro. Sin embargo, cuando surgió la posibilidad de incorporar a Rodri, el club no dudó en valorar la operación. La decisión respondía a dos motivos. Por un lado, la entidad azulgrana tenía la oportunidad de sumar a uno de los mejores centrocampista del mundo. Por otro, encontraba en él un perfil capaz de aportar experiencia, personalidad y liderazgo a un vestuario con numerosos jugadores jóvenes. La llegada del madrileño suponía, por tanto, una apuesta que trascendía lo estrictamente futbolístico. Su trayectoria y su carácter podían ser claves dentro de una plantilla muy joven que necesita referentes tanto en los buenos momentos como cuando los resultados no acompañan. Y el internacional ha asumido, con éxito, el rol. A nivel social, desde el primer día que llegó, precisamente para la disputa del trofeo Joan Gamper, el Spotify Camp Nou ya le recibió con una sonora ovación. Además, es una pieza clave e intocable en el once de Flick.

articles.title: Ivan Toney: England striker nightclub assault trial set for 2028
articles.summary: The footballer has denied assaulting a man at a Soho nightclub on 6 December last year.
articles.body:
England striker Ivan Toney will face trial in 2028 over the alleged assault of a man at a central London nightclub.

The 30-year-old footballer, from Northampton, previously pleaded not guilty to attacking Saber Da Silva at a nightclub in Wardour Street, Soho, on 6 December 2025.

He formally entered this plea at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday, where a provisional trial date was set for the same court of 12 June 2028.

Judge Christopher Hehir told the defendant he was "sorry" about the delay, adding: "As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons."

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Da Silva during a confrontation at the 100 Wardour Street club.

The criminal case came after a Metropolitan Police investigation and the charge was announced in July.

Toney, who represented England at this summer's World Cup, was released on unconditional bail after the hearing on Thursday.

His provisional trial date of 12 June 2028 falls during the group stages of the men's European Championship, which is being jointly hosted by England, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

articles.title: Guillem Víctor llama a la puerta
articles.standfirst: Ante la ausencia de Koundé, el canterano se ejercitó este jueves a las órdenes de Flick
articles.summary: Ante la ausencia de Koundé, el canterano se ejercitó este jueves a las órdenes de Flick
articles.body: Guillem Víctor fue la principal novedad en la sesión de entrenamiento de este jueves del Barcelona. La presencia del lateral derecho del filial responde a la ausencia de Koundé, ya que el francés sigue sin recuperarse del esguince de tobillo y está prácticamente descartado para el choque contra el Alavés. Por lo tanto, el canterano tiene muchas opciones de entrar en la lista de convocados para este sábado. Nacido el 3 de mayo de 2007 en Sant Cugat y hermano del exculé Pau Víctor, actualmente en el Braga, llegó al fútbol base del Barcelona en categoría alevín procedente del Júnior. En la temporada 2024-25, como juvenil de segundo año, empezó a tener un papel minutos con el Juvenil A, con 18 partidos de Liga, tres de Youth League y dos de Copa del Rey. El curso pasado fue uno de los capitanes del Juvenil A e incluso debutó con el filial. Esta temporada es una pieza clave del Barça Atlètic. Ha sido titular y ha completado todos los minutos en los siete últimos compromisos del filial. No es la primera vez que el lateral derecho se ejercita con el primer equipo. Xavi Hernández ya le llamó en 2023 y, el año pasado, también fue citado por Hansi Flick para alguna sesión. Además, durante el último parón por compromisos internacionales, el técnico alemán volvió a contar con los servicios del zaguero en un entrenamiento. Guillem Víctor es un lateral derecho con buen toque de balón, aunque también destaca por su polivalencia. Puede ocupar posiciones en el centro del campo y, como interior, tiene llegada al área. A la espera del entrenamiento de mañana viernes, el catalán tiene opciones de entrar en su primera convocatoria con el Barcelona. Àlex Campos, por su parte, sigue en dinámica del primer equipo. El central, que ya ha sido convocado para los dos últimos compromisos, apunta a entrar también en la lista para el partido contra el Alavés. Hansi Flick tiene las bajas de Eric García, Xavi Espart y Christensen y, probablemente, tampoco podrá contar con Koundé en la zaga.

articles.title: Turrientes: "San Mamés será difícil, pero queremos seguir nuestra buena dinámica con tres puntos"
articles.standfirst: El de Beasain afronta con optimismo el derbi del domingo en Bilbao, por la buena dinámica de la Real y porque se ha estrenado como goleador en Europa y en Liga
articles.summary: El de Beasain afronta con optimismo el derbi del domingo en Bilbao, por la buena dinámica de la Real y porque se ha estrenado como goleador en Europa y en Liga
articles.body: Beñat Turrientes desea que la Real Sociedad pueda continuar el domingo en San Mamés la buena trayectoria que está llevando en las últimas semanas y vuelva de Bilbao con un triunfo muy valioso a nivel de clasificación y también de moral. En este sentido, el de Beasain está contento de marcar el otro día ante el Levante su primer gol en Primera, como destacamos en MARCA. Turrientes, como toda la Real, afronta positivo el derbi de domingo. “Estamos en un dinámica muy buena, pero sabemos que el domingo en San Mamés vamos a tener un partido muy difícil y lo estamos preparando bien, porque queremos seguir con esa buena trayectoria y vamos a ir a por los tres puntos. El derbi siempre es especial, importante para nosotros y nuestras aficiones, sabemos que allí siempre son partidos difíciles, pero hemos ganado los últimos y quereos seguir en esa línea”. La Real llega en un gran momento a la cita de San Mamés. “Cuando el equipo está en buena dinámica y juega bien al fútbol vas de otra manera a los partidos, pero yo creo que en estos partidos no hay favorito, los derbis hay que jugarlos. Yo creo que va a ser un partido bonito, ellos van a salir muy motivados, nosotros también, vamos a ir allí a por los tres puntos”. Le han comentado que, como en su día publicamos en MARCA, está habiendo más goleadores distintos que nunca, hasta 13 a día de hoy. “Eso dice el nivel que hay en todas las posiciones y que todos sumamos. Queremos seguir así”. Ese dato puede llegar porque todos los futbolistas están teniendo sus partidos, por las rotaciones que está llevando a cabo Matarazzo. ¿Cómo lleva un futbolista no jugar algunos días, cuando tiene el deseo de hacerlo siempre? “Es verdad que todos queremos jugar siempre, pero tenemos que darnos cuenta de que hay muchos partidos y mucha competencia. Se trata de que, cuando te toque,lo hagas bien y se sume entre todos”. La Real está marcando muchos goles, pero también recibiéndolos. Por ello, los derbis de la pasada temporada en Copa, con 0-1 y 1-0, pueden ser los que hay que seguir. “Es verdad que el partido de Copa fue muy completo en todos los aspectos y lo queremos repetir. Creo que contra el Levante se vio en la segunda parte que, en el aspecto de controlar los partidos, el equipo ha mejorado mucho”. En el 0-1 él fue el autor de gol. “Fue un momento muy especial, meter un gol en un derbi y en semifinales de Copa. Fue un gran momento para mí, para familia y amigos”. Le hemos destacado que llega al derbi después de, por fin, marcar un gol en Liga, pocos días después de estrenarse también en Europa. “La verdad que tenía en Liga tenía esa espina de que todavía no había metido en Liga, parece que cuando metes un viene más, así que por esa parte contento. ¿Aportar más dianas? Soy un jugador box to box, me gusta llegar al área, tengo buen golpeo, me lo dicen y yo lo sé, ahora que he metido uno a ver si llegan más”.

articles.title: El Cuti no pierde el tiempo
articles.standfirst: El argentino completó la sesión con el grupo y podría ser titular ante el Levante
articles.summary: El argentino completó la sesión con el grupo y podría ser titular ante el Levante
articles.body: Dos partidos se ha perdido el Cuti Romero desde que se marchase tocado ante el Espanyol. Suficientes para ver que el equipo es otro sin el argentino sobre el césped. Y no es cosa de resultados, puesto que los rojiblancos sacaron un punto con diez en Alemania y ganaron al Deportivo dejando la portería a cero. Pero en ambos duelos notaron la ausencia del jefe de la defensa. Tras incorporarse el martes a los entrenamientos, el central ya mira a Levante como posible titular. Y es que Simeone no quiere probaturas en uno de los campos en los que peor recuerdo tiene. El míster argentino probó con su compatriota en el centro de la zaga formando pareja con Hancko. Muestra suficiente del nivel de importancia que tiene el choque del sábado. La presencia del Cuti como posible titular es una gran noticia para el Atlético que con el argentino desde el inicio solo conoce la victoria en LaLiga. Tan solo en Anfield cayeron derrotados con Cristian de titular. La jerarquía del de Córdoba se ha notado desde el primer día que puso los pies sobre el verde vestido de rojiblanco. En su estreno en Liga frente al Athletic en San Mamés entró al campo con el partido ya muy cuesta arriba. Pero desde entonces suma cinco triunfos con tres porterías a cero. De hecho, podríamos sumar cuatro porterías a cero si recordásemos que en el derbi se marchó del campo en el minuto 89 sin haber encajado. El tanto que recibió Oblak fue minutos después de marcharse el Cuti del césped. Números que demuestran que desde el primer momento se ha convertido en una pieza clave. Ante el Espanyol tuvo que retirarse cuando faltaban algo más de 20 minutos para acabar el choque por un problema físico que le dejó fuera de combate ante Stuttgart y Deportivo. Ahora, a unos días de comenzar una semana clave, el argentino no quiere perder el tiempo y se postula como titular frente al Levante. Gran noticia para el Cholo sabiendo que con Cuti sobre el campo el Atlético recibe gol cada 150 minutos. En los 602’ que estuvo sobre el césped, los rojiblancos tan solo encajaron cuatro tantos. Cifras que permiten a los colchoneros recuperar una solidez que parecía perdida. Pero no sólo el Atlético mejoró defensivamente con el Cuti en el campo, es que el argentino es clave a la hora de iniciar las jugadas. Algo que los rojiblancos echaron en falta en sus últimos dos partidos para salir con la pelota. El regreso de Cristian permite a Simeone recuperar esa seguridad atrás y tener al hombre que inicia todos los ataques. Una recuperación que llega justo en el momento clave. El Cuti parece listo para visitar Valencia y liderar al Atlético ante el Levante.

articles.title: Sarabia se despide de Elche rumbo al Espanyol: "Hemos sido tremendamente felices"
articles.standfirst: El técnico firma hasta 2028 y toma el relevo de Manolo González, con los pericos en descenso y eliminados de la Copa
articles.summary: El técnico firma hasta 2028 y toma el relevo de Manolo González, con los pericos en descenso y eliminados de la Copa
articles.body: Eder Sarabia cambia de banquillo sin olvidarse de Elche. El nuevo entrenador del RCD Espanyol, que firma hasta 2028, ha dedicado un mensaje de despedida a la ciudad en la que consiguió un ascenso a Primera y una sufrida permanencia. "Aquí empezó todo y aquí termina", ha publicado en Instagram junto a una imagen en bicicleta desde la Ermita de San Pascual, en Orito. El bilbaíno, que todavía residía allí con su familia, ha acompañado la fotografía con otra frase: "Hemos sido tremendamente felices". Su siguiente destino le exige una respuesta inmediata. Sarabia sustituye al destituido Manolo González y se hace cargo de un Espanyol en puestos de descenso y recién eliminado de la Copa por el Sestao River, de Segunda RFEF. Será su primera experiencia en un banquillo desde que dejó el Elche el pasado mes de mayo, después de asegurar la salvación en Girona. Aquella permanencia fue su último servicio al conjunto franjiverde. Sarabia decidió marcharse cuando aún le quedaba un año de contrato y cerró una etapa en la que llevó al equipo desde Segunda hasta la continuidad en la élite. Su regreso a los banquillos ha provocado reacciones diversas entre los aficionados del Elche: unos le agradecen su trabajo y le desean suerte; otros cuestionan los motivos que expuso para justificar su salida del Martínez Valero. Dos partidos de sanción pendientes El reencuentro con el Elche llegará en la segunda vuelta, cuando el Espanyol visite el Martínez Valero. Los dos equipos ya se enfrentaron esta temporada en el RCDE Stadium, en un encuentro que terminó con la primera victoria del curso para el conjunto de Martín Anselmi. Sarabia tendrá que esperar para dirigir a su nuevo equipo desde la banda. El técnico arrastra dos partidos de sanción por su expulsión en La Cartuja en la antepenúltima jornada de la pasada temporada.

articles.title: Premier League to League One - is double drop becoming more common?
articles.summary: Back-to-back relegations to the third tier of English football are becoming more common and this season Burnley could make it a hat-trick after Luton Town and Leicester.
articles.body:
One day Leicester were playing Liverpool in the Premier League, then within 15 months it was Notts County, Burton Albion and MK Dons in League One.

It is a path of back-to-back relegations to the third tier of English football which was exceptionally rare. Now statistically it is becoming more common.

With Burnley marooned in the Championship relegation zone, they could be the third team in three years to suffer the double drop

For the 1,450 Burnley supporters who made the trip to Lincoln City last weekend, the threat is all too real.

Head coach Nicky Hayen was never likely to survive a 4-1 defeat by a Lincoln team who were in non-league football 10 years ago.

With Diego Lopez appointed as Burnley's new chief football officer , and Fabio Celestini installed as their new boss , the Clarets must now hope for a change in fortunes.

Is the Championship becoming ever-more competitive as well-run clubs like Lincoln make an impact?

Or it simply a case of clubs from the Premier League imploding after relegation?

Fifteen years ago, the suggestion a top-flight club could be relegated in successive seasons was unthinkable.

After all, in the first 20 seasons of the Premier League it happened just the once.

That was to Swindon Town, and even then there were special circumstances.

The Robins finished fourth bottom of the second tier in 1994-95 but were relegated because of the rebalancing of the divisions to reduce the Premier League to 20 teams.

In any other season they would not have suffered the double drop.

As such, it could be argued that Wolves were the first team to suffer a double drop from the Premier League after being relegated in 2011-12.

Since then it has happened four times in 14 seasons.

Or, after Sunderland went down in 2016-18, three times in nine seasons.

And then back-to-back seasons with Luton and Leicester.

Meanwhile, Wigan and Portsmouth were relegated to League One after a second season in the Championship, Leeds and Sheffield Wednesday after a third.

For Wolves, Sunderland and Leicester there was considerable turmoil on and off the pitch which contributed to their demise.

During their double drop descent, Wolves - who remarkably suffered a treble drop to the bottom tier in the 1980s - burned through four managers and made a series of poor transfers.

Sunderland did so with the ignominy of being the only club to finish bottom of both divisions, winning just 13 of 84 league matches.

The Black Cats had been in the top flight for 10 seasons - though they had only reached the 40-point barrier, usually the target to remain in the division, three times.

Leicester's relegation to League One was a direct result of poor boardroom decisions, with a six-point deduction for breaching profit and sustainability regulations ultimately sealing their fate. The Foxes finished 23rd in the Championship, five points from safety.

It took Sunderland four years to return to the Championship, and such is the turmoil at Leicester an immediate promotion looks unlikely. Russell Martin's Leicester side sit 11th in League One, with the club up for sale.

"Despite the fact we've seen Luton and Leicester suffer back-to-back relegations in recent years, I don't see it as a trend that will continue," former Watford and Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff, now an EFL pundit, told BBC Sport.

"For both of those clubs, in my opinion, it was a case of mismanagement of the playing squad.

"From Luton's perspective, there were a few players there who maybe felt an entitlement to stay in the Premier League. They didn't readjust to being back at the Championship, where most of their players had actually been previously.

"And for Leicester City, they kept hold of too many that didn't really want to be there and then obviously weren't equipped to deal with a relegation battle."

While Luton may have got their recruitment wrong, they were much more responsibly run compared to the other double drop clubs.

The Hatters' progress off the pitch remains progressive rather than regressive, with work advancing on a new 25,000-capacity stadium at Power Court which is due to be completed for the start of 2028-29.

The fine line for success is shown by Luton's relegation from the Championship in 2024-25. They went down because of their inferior goal difference compared to Hull City , with the Tigers then promoted to the Premier League the following season.

Championship will become 'a much more competitive league'

Burnley had earned a reputation as the archetypal yo-yo club - relegated from or promoted to the top division in each of the past five seasons.

But after a leveraged buyout by Alan Pace's ALK Capital in 2020, the Clarets were carrying £142m in loans in the 2024-25 accounts - the year they went up - which was the highest debt level in the Championship.

This week Burnley set a new English league record for the longest run without a home win. When they host Portsmouth on Saturday, it will be 378 days since their last home victory.

Being humbled by a well-run, up-and-coming club like Lincoln, with far fewer resources but savvy ownership, will not be lost on Burnley supporters.

Burnley's total revenue for 2024-25 was £71.7m, which dwarfed Lincoln's £7.81m.

The Clarets then received £48m in parachute payments. Lincoln can expect about £5.5m in solidarity funding.

Off the pitch there should be no contest, but football is not played purely on balance sheets.

In its State of the Game report, published earlier this month, the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) said a new financial deal between the Premier League and the EFL must "reduce the distortive impact that parachute payments have on financial incentives within the Championship".

The solution is merit payments, which would mirror the Premier League's model of prize money by final league position.

At present, every club in the Championship receives the same payment, regardless of where they finish.

"The amount of money paid in parachute payments will reduce and the amount of money going into the Championship will vastly increase," IFR chair David Kogan said.

"The delta between parachute payment clubs and non-parachute payment clubs is going to significantly reduce, which makes the Championship a much more competitive league."

Parachute payments are paid to clubs relegated from the Premier League to help them adjust to the financial realities of the second tier - £48m in year one, then £39m in year two

Could this make the double drop more common as the revenue gap closes? Much will depend upon just how "significantly" the gap is closed.

The IFR report found that parachute payment clubs were more than four times more likely to be promoted. In 2024-25, four clubs were in receipt and they were almost 27 points better off, and filled the top three places (with Luton relegated).

"If you look at the numbers of teams that go back up or finish in the top places, there's a huge correlation between those clubs and the ones that are parachute payment clubs," McAnuff said.

"Even with a reduction in parachute payments, I still feel that advantage will prove to be massively significant for those teams.⁠​⁠‍⁠"

It may yet be that Burnley escape the double drop, that the financial advantage of parachute payments outweighs poor decision-making.

But the double drop has generally become far more common. And that should concern any club that gets relegated and is not prepared for life in the Championship.

articles.title: Mbangula desentierra un 'hat-trick' único que tenía la marca registrada de Batistuta: "Ojalá no sea el último"
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Bolonia es el primero que marca tres goles al Milan en San Siro desde 'Batigol'
articles.summary: El extremo del Bolonia es el primero que marca tres goles al Milan en San Siro desde 'Batigol'
articles.body: Samuel-Germain Kinduelu Mbangula Tshifunda (Bruselas, 2004) creció con la vitola de ser una de las grandes promesas de las 'Next Gen' de la Juventus. La 'Vecchia Signora', sin ir más lejos, pagó 390.000 euros al Anderlecht por su traspaso en 2020. Sus destellos desde que Thiago Motta le hiciera debutar con el primer equipo en 2024 -marcó cuatro goles y repartió cinco asistencias en 32 partidos- le valieron para convertirse en el segundo fichaje más caro (10 millones) en la historia del Werder Bremen. "Necesitábamos incorporar jugadores más jóvenes y convertirlos en activos importantes. Mangula creemos que tiene un gran potencial desde el punto de vista futbolístico, pero también más adelante, quizá nos pueda dar réditos en el mercado de fichajes", aseguraba Klaus Filbry, director general del club, en una 'mesa redonda' con MARCA. No cuajó -registró tres tantos y cuatro pases de gol en 28 partidos- y el Bolonia optó por 'repescarle' cedido con una opción de compra valorada en 12,5 millones de euros. En el Renato Dall'Ara tampoco entró con buen pie. Suplente tanto con Domenico Tedesco como en los inicios de Raffaele Palladino, el ex de la Juve aprovechó su primera titularidad -apenas había acumulado 14 minutos en tres partidos- para reivindicarse por todo lo alto. En realidad se convirtió en héroe por accidente. Mbangula se coló en el once por las lesiones de Orsolini, Piccoli, Enem y Cambiaghi y acabó dinamitando al Milan (2-4) con un 'hat-trick' histórico. Según 'Opta', desde que se instauraron los tres puntos por victoria en Serie A (1994-95), sólo Gabriel Omar Batistuta (1998) había anotado tres goles en San Siro jugando de visitante... contra el Milan. Palabras mayores. El belga, internacional sub 21, 'abrió la lata' en el 8' al rematar de primeras un centro atrás de Nadir Zortea, puso el 2-3 en el 62' al solventar con una gran maniobra un pase filtrado por el español Juan Miranda y anotó el definitivo 2-4 en el 86' al culminar en boca de gol un envío de Jens Odgaard. Ponía fin así a casi un año de sequía: 355 días para ser exactos. No marcaba desde el 7 de noviembre de 2025, cuando anotó el gol de la victoria en el 94' contra el Wolfsburgo (2-1). Se hizo esperar... pero valió la pena. "Es una de las mejores noches de mi vida. Es mi primer hat-trick, pero espero que no sea el último. Hacerlo en San Siro es un plus, porque es un estadio muy difícil. Siento la confianza que el entrenador tiene en mí y eso es importante. Somos un buen grupo, y ésa es nuestra verdadera fortaleza: siempre estamos unidos, y lo hemos demostrado sin rendirnos jamás", reconocía Mbangula. Su 'tripletta', sin embargo, podría cambiar su suerte a las órdenes de Palladino. "No había jugado mucho hasta ahora, pero incluso antes de los tres goles, me gustó su entrega: incluso defendió por la banda derecha en los últimos minutos", reconocía el técnico del Bolonia. San Siro puede haber alumbrado el nacimiento de una nueva estrella. Veremos...

articles.title: Dundee: How Pressley's 'jobby team' are defying expectations to sit fourth
articles.summary: Steven Pressley has Dundee soaring high in fourth place in the Scottish Premiership after the first round of fixtures, but how has he done it?
articles.body:
Steven Pressley did not make a terrific first impression as Dundee manager.

"If you look through a certain lens and you're looking for a manager with a history of winning titles, I'm not your man," he told the media at his unveiling in June last year.

This was the unwavering honesty Pressley has brought to the job, but back then, it was not particularly well received in the ruthless world of Scottish football.

The former Scotland defender was many punters' favourite to be the season's first managerial sacking. His team were criticised after a rocky start. His interviews were pilloried. Even his choice of matchday attire was widely lampooned.

Sixteen months on, nobody is laughing anymore.

'Big Elvis' has Dundee soaring high in fourth place in the Scottish Premiership after the first round of fixtures, just three points behind Hearts, the darlings of last season. And Hearts, remember, needed goals in the 84th and 96th minutes to down Pressley's men at Tynecastle last month.

How has this happened? And can Dundee maintain their momentum?

Dundee have made Dens Park a fortress this season. Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw. Motherwell, Aberdeen and - in a madcap final 10 minutes on Wednesday - Kilmarnock have all been dispatched on league business.

Only Hibernian have taken three points from Dundee's back yard.

That's not to say Pressley's troops have toiled on their travels. They were impressive at Celtic Park in a 1-0 defeat on the opening day and claimed the city spoils with a 2-0 triumph down the road at Tannadice.

Underpinning this has been tactical flexibility and a workmanlike industry in the image of their studious figurehead. The players have clarity in their roles and are asked to run their legs off.

The 3-1 victory over Kilmarnock was a case in point. Pegged back to 1-1 by Joe Hugill's penalty and having seemingly ceded the impetus, Dundee regrouped and seized back control.

"The thing that really pleased me was after Kilmarnock scored and the momentum changed, we showed great resilience and determination and ran really hard," Pressley told BBC Scotland.

"After the equaliser it is easy to feel sorry for yourselves. We didn't and we got a really important three points."

Pressley has weathered the sale of big assets and injuries to key players too. Tony Yogane went north to Aberdeen, having been a profitable option down the left. Luke Graham and Billy Koumetio left a gaping chasm at the heart of the Dundee defence and the dangerous Cam Congreve went back to parent club Swansea City.

To stretch Dundee yet further, veteran striker and club icon Simon Murray was seriously injured at the start of the campaign. Joe Westley, who scored nine goals last season, has been out for a month. Yet another forward – Bobby Wales – is injured too, as are Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse.

Pressley has recruited shrewdly from the English market to stem the bleeding.

Matia Akinmombi got his introduction to the Scottish game this week. Fellow Bournemouth loanee Owen Bevan has brought class and composure to the backline. Bradley Fink, on loan from Wycombe Wanderers, has scored four goals in six matches.

Ever the honest man, Pressley admitted he did not see such a lofty position coming just over a year into the job.

There are moneyed clubs with a January window around the corner, yet nothing to suggest Dundee will run out of gas.

Westley has now returned to fitness, new signings are getting to grips with the freneticism of the Scottish top flight and the club's trajectory continues to rise.

Wednesday at Dens marked the 11th match of the season and the completion of a full round of Premiership fixtures. In other words, Dundee have played every other club in the league and defied any lingering pre-season pessimism.

They have respite to build and grow anew, before travelling to St Johnstone a week on Saturday.

Then it's Hearts at home and potentially a chance to draw level with the Edinburgh side, before a trip to Easter Road and a Hibernian team whose form has plummeted since their storming of Dens.

And so here Dundee are, clinging on to the top three, with a manager who is fast attaining cult hero status among his fanbase and hard-won respect from the rest of the division.

To borrow another of Pressley's famous remarks: "Not bad for a 'jobby' team."

articles.title: Neville says managers need sacking ‘for own good’ as Man Utd retain Carrick
articles.summary: Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville believes root of team’s problems is Glazer family, urges them to sell up.
articles.body:
Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to be dismissed “for their own good” as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win.

Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

But Carrick, 45, and a former United and England midfielder, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match news conference later on Thursday ahead of the team’s league match away to Chelsea on Saturday.

“I reckon what’s happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that [the United hierarchy] literally debated [Carrick’s future] back and forth,” former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast.

“I don’t know this, but they’ve debated it to the point where they’ve got themselves into a muddle, and thought, ‘we’ll just stay with him’.”

“I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That’s when you’re really struggling.”

Neville, a former United teammate of Carrick, added: “Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery.”

Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford.

Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth.

Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch, as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s current malaise.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

Neville believes the root of United’s woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying “enough is enough” as he urged them to sell up.

The Glazers took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005. They remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to British billionaire businessman Jim Ratcliffe in 2024.

Neville, a longstanding critic, reiterated his call for the United States-based family to sell.

“There’s 1.2 billion pounds [$1.6 billion] of debt in that football club, they’re hamstrung in some ways,” said Neville, adding: “You’ve got a failure of 13, 14 years on the football side, you’ve subbed it out to somebody else [Ratcliffe] which is ridiculous, and not took responsibility … Enough is enough, they have to sell the whole club.”

“The fans have had enough. They have to go now.”

articles.title: Cristiano celebra su ‘Balón de Oro de Todos los Tiempos’: "¡El fútbol pertenece a los aficionados!"
articles.standfirst: El portugués agradece el respaldo recibido en la votación popular que ha elegido su Balón de Oro de 2008 por delante del de Messi de 2012
articles.summary: El portugués agradece el respaldo recibido en la votación popular que ha elegido su Balón de Oro de 2008 por delante del de Messi de 2012
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo ha querido compartir con sus seguidores un reconocimiento que le devuelve al principio de su colección de Balones de Oro. El portugués ha celebrado en X el resultado del B.O.A.T. (Ballon d’Or of All Time), la consulta popular organizada por el Balón de Oro para elegir la mejor edición ganadora de su historia. La elegida ha sido la suya de 2008, conquistada cuando vestía la camiseta del Manchester United. "¡El fútbol pertenece a los aficionados! Gracias a todos los aficionados del mundo, el Balón de Oro de Todos los Tiempos también es suyo", escribió Cristiano. Acompañó sus palabras con una fotografía de aquel primer galardón: un joven Ronaldo, de traje y corbata, besando el trofeo que inauguró su particular colección. El mensaje pone el foco en quienes han decidido el resultado. Los participantes en la consulta situaron su triunfo de 2008 por delante del Balón de Oro de Messi de 2012. El podio lo completó otra versión del propio Cristiano: la de 2017, cuando conquistó el último de sus cinco galardones, ya como jugador del Real Madrid. La imagen elegida para agradecer el apoyo remite a una temporada decisiva en su carrera. En la campaña 2007-08, Cristiano marcó 42 goles con el Manchester United, ganó la Premier League y conquistó la Champions. También fue suyo el tanto del equipo de Alex Ferguson en la final de Moscú contra el Chelsea, resuelta en la tanda de penaltis. Aquella actuación colectiva e individual le abrió las puertas de su primer Balón de Oro. La iniciativa tiene carácter conmemorativo: no añade un sexto Balón de Oro a su palmarés ni contempla la entrega de un trofeo físico. La consulta permitía participar mediante votos de pago y repetir la elección, una fórmula distinta a la que decide el premio anual. Cristiano ha celebrado ese respaldo con una dedicatoria directa. Casi dos décadas después de aquella fotografía, ha recuperado el recuerdo de su primera conquista para compartirlo con los aficionados que la han vuelto a colocar en lo más alto.

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick ready to 'move forward' with Bruno Fernandes as captain and doesn't require assurances on his own future
articles.summary: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick says there is "no decision to be made on" whether Bruno Fernandes remains as club captain; midfielder was benched for defeat to Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics; Carrick will take charge of Saturday's trip to Chelsea
articles.body:
Carrick benched Fernandes for Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth after the midfielder spoke out about his manager's tactics in the Champions League defeat at Como last week.

Sky Sports News reported Carrick and Fernandes held clear-the-air talks on Tuesday.

On Sunday, Carrick said the decision to name Fernandes among the subs was for "football" reasons and he stood by that statement on Thursday in a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League trip to Chelsea.

"It was a decision for the game. That's it," said Carrick. "Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I've got no issues with that, we move forward.

"We're looking forward to the game now."

On whether Fernandes would continue as captain after Harry Maguire took the armband last weekend, Carrick said: "There's no decision to be made on that."

Carrick was then asked whether Fernandes was too emotional to be captain and gave his clear backing to the 32-year-old.

"He's the captain of our football club," said Carrick. "There are different personalities, different characteristics, different ways to lead. It all comes down to what happens on the football pitch and whether you win or not in the end.

"He cares deeply about this football club and the team and he's desperate to do well. We'll lead that together."

Carrick: I don't need assurances on my future

Carrick's future as Man Utd head coach has been in the spotlight since the defeat at home to Bournemouth extended the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met at the club's Carrington training ground this week to discuss next steps but Carrick will continue to lead the team.

Despite the noise around his position, Carrick has insisted he doesn't require guarantees from the hierarchy about his long-term security.

"I don't need assurances from anyone," he said in Thursday's press conference. "I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that. I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."

Carrick said his "main focus" has been preparing for Chelsea and he is not tuned in to criticism or questions about his future in the media.

"I don't see it," he said. "I only see the things I need to see.

"I don't look for it. It doesn't help. I've said it before, I care about what the supporters think. I care about how it feels in the stadium and them travelling to games - I care about what we give them and what they see.

"I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job and I know what we need to be better. I don't need anyone else to tell me."

Asked if he was surprised to still be in his position, Carrick said: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team. I'm desperate to make things better and improve things. I'm not surprised, no."

Analysis: Cool Carrick delivers message of togetherness

"He handled himself very well. He was very cool, he was very calm, he was very self-assured.

"The message he was trying to send out was: 'we at this club are going to stick together, I'm going to stick together with the players, the players are hurting, we accept performances and results haven't been good enough but we're working hard to turn things around'.

"I got the sense Carrick didn't want to talk too much about Fernandes. But we know he's had clear-the-air talks with Fernandes and it seems he will remain as captain.

"When it comes to handling the media, Carrick is the ultimate safe pair of hands because of his experience at the highest level being a player. He knows how things can be spun and blown up out of proportion.

"His message is always 'this is not about me, it's all about Man Utd, the club'."

articles.title: Chupete y una Copa trampolín
articles.standfirst: Su doblete en Copa anima al delantero
articles.summary: Su doblete en Copa anima al delantero
articles.body: Chupete fue, sin duda, uno de los grandes nombres propios del Málaga CF en su estreno copero ante el Sporting de Alcázar. El delantero cordobés saltó al terreno de juego tras el descanso y terminó siendo decisivo con un doblete, los dos primeros tantos de los tres que acabó marcando el conjunto blanquiazul. Primero, desde el punto de penalti en el minuto 70. Después, definiendo con la pierna izquierda dentro del área tras una buena asistencia de Izan Merino. El atacante malaguista necesitaba una noche así. Chupete entró al campo en el descanso después de una primera mitad gris del Málaga, que se marchó al vestuario sin un solo lanzamiento entre los tres palos, y respondió de la mejor manera posible: con goles. El cordobés llevaba dos meses sin ver puerta, desde la segunda jornada de LaLiga, cuando también marcó de penalti ante el RC Deportivo de La Coruña en La Rosaleda. Durante este periodo, Chupete había mostrado cierta ansiedad de cara a portería, mientras veía cómo Adrián Niño, su principal competencia por el puesto, encontraba con mayor facilidad el camino del gol. Por eso, su actuación en Alcázar de San Juan tiene un valor añadido. Más aún después del penalti que el delantero había fallado recientemente ante el Levante UD. Esta vez no hubo dudas desde los once metros. Pero el doblete tiene también un componente estadístico que conecta directamente con la versión más letal de Chupete. El delantero volvió a firmar dos goles en un mismo encuentro, una de las grandes señas de identidad de su espectacular temporada pasada. El curso anterior, el ariete malaguista consiguió nueve dobletes, dentro de una campaña en la que alcanzó las 25 dianas. Aquellos números situaron a Chupete como uno de los grandes especialistas del gol múltiple en el fútbol mundial. De hecho, fue el futbolista que más encuentros con dos o más tantos acumuló entre las 59 ligas con mayor coeficiente del mundo, por delante de jugadores como Erling Haaland o Harry Kane. Además, superó el récord de David Villa como el jugador menor de 22 años con más dobletes en la historia de Segunda División. En Alcázar, Chupete volvió a encontrarse con una versión de sí mismo que el Málaga necesitaba recuperar. Dos goles, confianza renovada y una reivindicación en el momento oportuno.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain, says Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick confirms Bruno Fernandes will remain captain, and addresses his own future before Saturday's trip to Chelsea.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is "fully committed" to the club and will continue as captain.

Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after the Portuguese questioned the tactics used in a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

The defeat by Bournemouth left Carrick's future hanging by a thread, but the 45-year-old will be in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea .

It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will return to the starting line-up, but the pair held clear-the-air talks at United's Carrington training ground on Tuesday in a bid to move forward.

Carrick says there is "no decision to be made" over whether Fernandes remains captain.

"We are clear with the situation of the team, and as a football club," said Carrick.

"He [Fernandes] is an important player for this group. He has been and he will be.

"We've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction.

"He's fully committed to this football club; he's fully committed to making things better. There are absolutely no issues with that.

"It doesn't change for me. It was a decision for what we felt for the [ Bournemouth ] game. That's it.

"He's the one that's led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that. There are absolutely no issues with that."

Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks

Carrick 'doesn't need assurances' over future

United have gone eight games without a win as they head to Chelsea - their worst run of results since 2015-16.

Not since the 1988-89 campaign have they had a sequence of nine matches without a win.

Nearly 40 hours passed between United losing against Bournemouth on Sunday and the club providing clarification on Carrick's future, with the Englishman being given a chance to turn things around at Old Trafford.

Talks involving the Glazer family, minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox took place before Carrick's immediate future was confirmed.

It seems likely he will remain in post for next Tuesday's Champions League match against Roma, and the Premier League encounter with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on 8 November, after which there is a two-week international break.

Carrick, though, says he does not need guarantees over his position.

"I don't need any assurances from anyone," he said.

"I totally get the position. I understand the job. I understand the responsibilities. I understand what comes with that. So, I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."

Asked if he was surprised to still be in a job, Carrick said: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team, and I'm desperate to make us better and improve things. So, I'm not surprised, no."

articles.title: Max Dowman: Arsenal's appeal against teenager's red card in Fleetwood Town defeat rejected
articles.summary: Max Dowman was sent off for kicking out at Harrison Neal after a heavy tackle during Arsenal's Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town on Tuesday; 16-year-old's reaction was adjudged to be violent conduct, meaning a three-game suspension
articles.body:
Dowman was dismissed in the second half for violent conduct after kicking out at Fleetwood's Harrison Neal following a heavy challenge, before Arsenal were knocked out of the Carabao Cup on penalties.

The 16-year-old will now miss Arsenal's next three domestic matches against Liverpool, Hull and Newcastle following the FA's decision to uphold the ban.

In a statement an FA spokesperson said an independent comission dismissed Arsenal's claims of "wronfgul dismissal and excessive punishment".

Arsenal potentially threadbare out wide at Liverpool

Arsenal's rejected appeal means they are down to the bare bones out wide ahead of Sunday's huge Premier League match at Liverpool - live on Sky Sports.

As things stand, Eberechi Eze is the only fit senior option for Mikel Arteta to call on at Anfield unless Noni Madueke recovers from the ankle injury which kept him out of Tuesday's shock defeat.

Summer-signing Christos Tzolis , who picked up a hamstring injury in the last international break, is closing in on a return but it remains to be seen if he will be deemed fit enough to return against Liverpool.

Bukayo Saka , meanwhile, is facing weeks out with a quadricep injury he suffered in the 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich earlier this month.

If Tzolis and Madueke are not ready to face Liverpool, Arteta may be forced to call on youngster Ceadach O'Neill , who impressed in moments against Fleetwood, but is yet to feature in the Premier League.

Versatile Kai Havertz could also be called upon to fill in out wide if Arteta decides to favour experience.

It is a blow for Dowman, whose opportunities have been limited this season, as Arsenal's current injury issues could have opened the door for him to make his first Premier League start of the seaosn.

Manager Arteta has given the teenager two appearances off the bench in the league, and one in the Champions League this season.

Dowman has started both of Arsenal's Carabao Cup matches, scoring twice against Ipswich in the third round before being sent off against Fleetwood.

Sky Sports News understands Arteta spoke to Dowman at length in the build-up to Arsenal's game against Fleetwood and told him what to expect from the League Two side.

He was told they would put in strong challenges and they would double up on him and was told repeatedly not to react.

Former Arsenal star Paul Merson has warned "superstar" Dowman that he must learn to cope with teams targeting him.

"My worry is because at Arsenal, and when you play for one of the big clubs, you get told once or twice, and that is it. Once or twice tops," said the Sky Sports pundit.

"And he's been told again. Obviously, Arteta's told him. He got sent off the other week for England against the USA. He's going to get that the whole of his career.

"The kid's a superstar already at 16 years of age. He was the one reason I was looking forward to watching the game. I was thinking, 'Please Dowman play, please Dowman play'.

"He's going to have that all the time now. He's going to be kicked. People are going to look at the game now, and they're going to go, 'Right, we've got to upset him. Try and get inside him. Try and upset him'.

"And he's got to be better than that. He got frustrated, and it's not always going to be easy. It's not always going to be a nine out of 10 every week. Sometimes he's going to have to go to the nitty-gritty and be a six or seven out of 10. Get back for the team. Might do a couple of special things in a game.

"You can't keep on being a superstar every game. Everybody has bad games. When you have bad games, you've got to make sure it doesn't affect the team as well, and you don't get sent off."

articles.title: Arsenal's Kai Havertz in goal drought so should Mikel Arteta keep faith in him ahead of Viktor Gyokeres against Liverpool?
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has a striker dilemma as Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres struggle to deliver goals; Arsenal's No 9s have scored fewer times than their defenders this season; watch Liverpool vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports from 3.30pm on Sunday; kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Arsenal's striker dilemma analysed 🔺Araujo helping shore up Liverpool 🔺A player to watch this weekend

While Alexander Isak heads into Sunday's game at Anfield having scored six goals for Liverpool this season, Arsenal's frontmen continue to misfire. Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres haven't hit a Premier League goal between them since early September.

Havertz has been Mikel Arteta's first choice since returning from injury last season. The 27-year-old started and scored in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in May and appeared to pick up where he left off in the new campaign.

After scoring in the Community Shield against Manchester City, Havertz added Premier League goals against Coventry and his former club Chelsea. Since then, though, he has played 561 minutes, more than nine hours, without finding the net in any competition.

Gyokeres finally broke his duck for the season in Tuesday's Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out loss to Fleetwood Town when he bundled in Arsenal's equaliser from close range. But it has been a struggle for him to even produce shots never mind goals.

Gyokeres has only mustered one shot, a header which looped harmlessly into the air against Nottingham Forest, in 148 Premier League minutes. The Sweden international hasn't registered any shots at all in his 160 minutes in the Champions League.

For the most part, the lack of goals from Arsenal's strikers hasn't mattered. They sit level on points with City at the top of the Premier League having won all but one of their eight games and have taken seven points from a possible nine in the Champions League.

But Arteta will be aware of just how tough it will be to continue their strong start to the season if they don't start to produce.

Nearly three months in, it is damning that Arsenal's defenders have scored more goals in all competitions than their strikers.

Sunday's meeting with Isak, a striker Arsenal coveted before his £125m move to Liverpool from Newcastle, is a reminder of what they lack. The club have built formidable resources in defence and midfield but still don't have a world-class goalscorer.

It is partly a result of how funds have been allocated.

The club have spent only £224.5m on forwards since Arteta's appointment, initially as head coach, in 2019 compared to £550.1m on midfielders and £350m on defenders.

Arsenal tried to address the issue in the summer. But after their unsuccessful pursuits of Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, they opted to stick with what they had, hoping Havertz could stay fit and Gyokeres could build on a 21-goal first season at the club.

Havertz's loss of form may have something to do with the hamstring injury he suffered on Germany duty but he was the main culprit for Arsenal's wasteful display against Fleetwood on Tuesday, when he was unable to score from seven shots.

His failure to capitalise frustrated Arsenal fans but his efforts called to mind comments by Brentford owner Matthew Benham earlier this year on how he assesses strikers. "For a striker, getting in position is way more informative than finishing," he said.

Benham believes that generating a high volume of chances is the biggest indicator of future success for a striker. And that is one area in which Gyokeres, who only had three shots to Havertz's seven against Fleetwood, has struggled at Arsenal.

Gyokeres has failed to register a shot in eight Premier League starts. It is the second-highest total of any out-and-out striker since the start of last season, behind only Randal Kolo Muani, who spent last term fighting relegation while on loan at Spurs.

Gyokeres can of course point to a decent scoring record. His 14 Premier League goals last season helped Arsenal win the title.

But none of them came against opponents of Liverpool's quality, which is why Arteta may hesitate to start him on Sunday.

A comparison between Gyokeres and Havertz's last two Premier League starts against Liverpool illustrates the differences in what they offer against top opposition.

Gyokeres didn't register a shot in either of his, which came in last season's 1-0 loss in August and the 0-0 draw in January. He had a combined total of just 25 touches, only four of which came in Liverpool's box. He only made 11 passes and won three duels.

Havertz didn't score in either of his last two starts against Liverpool either, in the 2-2 draw in October 2024 and the 3-1 win in February of the same year. But he caused problems in both, registering five shots worth 1.22 xG and having 14 touches in the box.

He also contributed far more in general play, as is typical. Havertz had 80 touches - more than three times as many as Gyokeres. He made considerably more passes, created more chances, won a far higher number of duels and won possession more times too.

Havertz's ability to combine with team-mates, interchange positions and help construct attacks makes Arsenal far more fluid in the final third and helps to explain why their open-play threat has increased this season, even as their striker's goal drought continues.

Arteta could opt for another player up front on Sunday. Mikel Merino is an option after proving his value as a makeshift striker. But Havertz remains the most likely candidate given the breadth of what he brings. A first goal since September would be timely.

Ronald Araujo will face Arsenal on Sunday having produced another excellent performance for Liverpool in their Carabao Cup win over Chelsea. The summer signing's resolute defending helped his side through. He made 10 of the team's 15 clearances.

He was similarly effective in their 2-0 win over Brighton last weekend, drawing roars of approval from fans at Anfield with his crunching tackles. "When you see someone like Ronald making challenges, being aggressive at the right times, everyone responds and that energy can help the team going forward," said Virgil van Dijk.

Araujo played in his natural position at centre-back against Chelsea but has mostly been used by Andoni Iraola at right-back. The size of his contribution to Liverpool's defensive efforts, even in a relatively unfamiliar role, can be seen in the numbers.

Iraola has also noted his offensive improvement. Araujo scored in Liverpool's Champions League wins over LASK and Villarreal and would have had a third goal against Chelsea if not for a superb save from Mike Penders. It all adds up to a positive impression.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Newcastle face Everton on Monday having beaten Crystal Palace thanks in part to full-back Amar Dedic , who had a hand in both goals and now has four assists in eight games this term.

Four Premier League games are live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Tottenham vs Crystal Palace on Saturday, kicking off at 5.30pm. Aston Villa then host Fulham at 8pm.

On Sunday, Liverpool vs Arsenal headlines the action, with kick-off at 4.30pm. The weekend's live coverage concludes on Monday Night Football , when Newcastle United take on Everton at 8pm.

Rio Ngumoha's unstoppable dribbling for Liverpool and Luka Vuskovic's vital role at Brighton were covered.
