articles.title: Muere Michel Pineda, mítico delantero del Espanyol y del Racing
articles.standfirst: Fue el autor del gol del ascenso a Primera de los cántabros en 1993; además jugó en Alavés y Lleida
articles.summary: Fue el autor del gol del ascenso a Primera de los cántabros en 1993
articles.body: El delantero hispano francés Michel Pineda ha fallecido a la edad de 62 años. El que fuera mítico futbolista del Espanyol y Racing ha muerto a temprana edad y el fútbol español le ha recordado. El espanyolismo está de luto por Pineda, que a finales de los años ochenta dio días de gloria en Sarrià y fue parte del Espanyol que en 1988 estuvo a punto de conquistar la Copa de la UEFA. El francés llegó del Auxerre en 1984 y defendió la camiseta blanquiazul hasta 1990 marcando 73 goles en todas las competiciones. Lo curioso es que luego se marchó al Racing y en la temporada 92-93 marcó el gol que dio el ascenso a Primera a los cántabros y envió a Segunda a los espanyolistas. Acabó su carrera en el Lleida y en el Alavés, por lo que fueron cuatro los clubes españoles en los que militó. Luego siguió ligado al Espanyol una vez retirado. Pineda era hispano francés y de hecho consiguió ser campeón de Europa sub 21 en el año 1986 con la selección española que dirigía Luis Suárez.

articles.title: Tottenham vs Crystal Palace: Have Spurs genuinely turned a corner in the Premier League under Roberto De Zerbi?
articles.summary: Spurs have been steadily improving under Roberto De Zerbi but it's been over 20 months since they won three league games in a row - might the curse be broken this weekend? Watch Spurs vs Crystal Palace live on Sky Sports Premier League on Saturday; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi is the latest boss to try his hand at the hat-trick. Wins over Coventry City and Chelsea have preceded this weekend's meeting with Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports . The elusive treble is within reach.

To right such a wrong would be a huge stepping stone for Spurs under De Zerbi. Not only would the result propel them into the top half of the table, but its potential to heal the wounded Spurs psyche would surely be invaluable.

Dr Tottenham have long been craving a healer of their own. A manager who is able to match stylistic promise with sound leadership. Many thought the pursuit of a fiery Italian known to be volatile in previous roles was a high-risk appointment, and yet the gamble had obvious growth potential. A way back from anonymity.

Instead of finding endless ways to lose games, either by shrinking from the fight or being unable to resist the temptation to self-destruct, Spurs have started to introduce discipline and control into their performances.

Finally, Tottenham have a tactical plan that works. There is structure and identity to their patterns of play, hunting in packs to adhere to De Zerbi's demands of an aggressive man-to-man press. Since he took charge in March, only three teams have forced more high turnovers (120) and won more possessions in the final third (72).

"I think we have suffered enough," De Zerbi said last Saturday after beating Chelsea at Stamford Bridge for the first time since April 2018, harking back to halcyon days under Mauricio Pochettino. "The results of the past are not our responsibility. We are working to change the mentality of our club."

Spurs trumping their rivals at the Bridge without conceding had not happened since December 1986, but of course the real power is in how De Zerbi legitimises what he describes as a "different Tottenham".

Two wins will not count for much if consolidation does not follow. Spurs need to prove themselves to be a collective that are no longer bullied out of results over a sustained period. One that has left the chaos of recent regimes in the past.

Key to that strategy is keeping their best players fit. A simple truth is that one of the north Londoners' greatest failings of recent seasons has been player availability. Just look what happens when 'special' James Maddison plays. Only Arsenal have won more Premier League points than Spurs since his return. That is no coincidence.

But something more has clicked. In their last three league outings, Spurs have run further and harder than in their opening five games, covering more ground and incorporating more high-speed running. Goals have begun to flow with better consistency, too, their conversion rate rising from 2.8 per cent to a much healthier 14 per cent.

And the defensive third is also showing signs of improvement. Spurs restricted Chelsea to seven shots and 31 per cent possession last weekend, only conceding 0.47 xG against. Since De Zerbi took post only Arsenal have a lower value xG against, which means the chances they give up are rarely ones with a high probability of an opponent scoring.

All of those facts are strategic successes for De Zerbi. With more refinement up top, in theory, Spurs should start to win games far more comfortably and in a manner that demonstrates the evolution of a team unified in approach and application.

The club signed 10 players at a cost of £320m in the summer to transform the manager's squad options but harmony cannot be bought. De Zerbi must foster that feeling himself.

De Zerbi is unlikely to get a better opportunity to prove a corner has been turned permanently. Will the three-in-a-row curse finally be broken?

articles.title: Rangers manager Derek McInnes defends Emmanuel Fernandez
articles.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes defends Emmanuel Fernandez, saying the centre-back "has been a big part of our better performances this season".
articles.body:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes has defended Emmanuel Fernandez, saying the centre-back "has been a big part" of their strong displays this term.

The Nigeria defender has come under some criticism after some high=profile mistakes, including during Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Hearts at Tynecastle in the Scottish Premiership.

The 25-year-old has started every match for Rangers, who have kept the most clean sheets in the league so far this season.

"I only get asked about Fernandez when he has a poor game. Nobody asked me about Fernandez on Saturday, he was outstanding on Saturday [against St Johnstone]," McInnes said before Saturday's League Cup semi-final against Aberdeen.

"Wednesday night wasn't on Manny Fernandez, Wednesday night was a collective.

"I never get asked about Manny when he does really well and he's been a big part of our better performances this season."

Rangers head to Hampden on Saturday - where Aberdeen await in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup - and McInnes is hoping to get the better of his old club.

Rangers have won three trophies since 2012 and have finished the last two seasons without any silverware.

McInnes, who took charge in June, is the latest manager charged with turning around that poor return and has the chance to make his mark, having defeated Celtic 3-0 in the quarter-finals at Ibrox.

"To get the first trophy would be so important, reinforcing confidence, reinforcing belief," the Rangers boss said.

"Traditionally, semi-finals can be fraught with a lot of nerves and tension and sometimes they're not the best games, because of what's at stake."

Aberdeen's poor form makes Rangers strong favourites to progress to December's final against either Hearts or Hibernian.

However, Dons boss Stephen Robinson did lift the trophy last term when in charge of St Mirren, and McInnes is wary of their opponents' ability to perform in a one-off game.

"They've got a good, experienced manager in Robbo and they've got some good players, experienced players, in Aberdeen and they'll be relishing the opportunity as well," McInnes added.

"People might view us as favourites for it and I understand that but we've' still got a game to win and Aberdeen are capable of a big performance.

"I'm just concentrating on us, if we get to our levels then hopefully it's going to be enough to win the game but a strong 90-minute performance is going to be required, I feel."

Sportsound: League Cup semi-final - Rangers v Aberdeen

While McInnes will be hoping to put one over on Robinson on Saturday, he admits he has "sympathy" for his fellow manager.

The Dons have lost three of their past four league matches, including Wednesday's 1-0 home defeat by Falkirk.

And McInnes commented: "I sympathise with all the managers, really, who feel that pressure.

"I've managed the club for eight years up there and it's not always an easy club to manage but they've got a good guy there and a guy who will get it right if given time, I have no doubts about it.

"I've obviously been to the national stadium quite a lot as a manager.

"I've managed St Johnstone, Kilmarnock and Aberdeen in semi-finals and we were never the favourites then but I always felt confident that we could win the game.

"So, I'm sure Aberdeen will feel the exact same confidence."

articles.title: Celtic and Rangers fail to overturn ban on supporters at next home Scottish Cup games after fan trouble at Ibrox
articles.summary: The Old Firm clubs will play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors following crowd trouble at their quarter-final fixture in March; Celtic and Rangers fans clashed on the pitch at Ibrox, and over 40 people were arrested
articles.body:
The Old Firm sides have also failed to successfully challenge the £100,000 fine they were ordered to pay their opponents for those games.

But the threat of a second match being played behind closed doors, which would have kicked in if there is any trouble at a Scottish Cup fixture before the end of next season, has been lifted.

The original sanction followed their quarter-final meeting last season that ended with fans from both sides clashing on the pitch at Ibrox .

Police Scotland arrested 43 people following the scenes that left officers injured as missiles and pyros were launched.

A Celtic statement read: "While we recognise that our appeal has been partially upheld, we remain extremely disappointed by this excessive and disproportionate punishment relating to an incursion by supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration.

"It continues to be our view that a false equivalence has been drawn in relation to the very different actions of two groups.

"We have not defended supporters entering the field of play and understand the part emotion plays in football. We would have expected this context and the very obvious distinction in behaviours to have been recognised.

"Additionally, the fact that Celtic Football Club had no responsibility for stadium safety arrangements also seems to have been disregarded in establishing these sanctions."

This was the first Old Firm game at Ibrox since 2018 where Celtic were given the full Broomloan Stand, meaning there were around 7,500 away fans at the game, while some broke into the away end before kick-off, too. The figure was in place to comply with Scottish Cup rules on ticket allocations.

The league match between Rangers and Celtic the previous weekend had around 2,500 away fans after an agreement between clubs to give around five per cent of stadium capacity to away teams for this fixture.

That followed seasons of reduced allocations or, at times, no away fans at all at games.

Celtic progressed to the semi-finals with a 4-2 shoot-out victory over Rangers after the goalless draw at Ibrox, which sparked a pitch invasion from both sets of supporters.

Some visiting fans spilled onto the playing surface to celebrate after the winning spot-kick and supporters from the Rangers end charged towards them, with fireworks thrown back and forth.

Following the sanction, Celtic said they were "shocked" by the "disproportionate punishment".

Rangers then allocated just 300 tickets to Celtic for their League Cup match at Ibrox this month .

The Ibrox side said that decision had been made based on the independent report that was commissioned following the Scottish Cup quarter-final in March.

They added that since that fixture in March "there have also been further pitch invasions involving Celtic supporters".

Celtic rejected the proposal, and it resulted in the SPFL intervening, with the determination being that no away fans would be permitted at Old Firm matches this season in the Scottish Premiership and League Cup.

An independent review into the scenes previously concluded that "crushing" and "life-threatening violence" was narrowly avoided.

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, found: "The Celtic Ultras were the first to enter the pitch in jubilation, with others following their lead.

"In contrast, the Union Bears' movement onto the track and towards the pitch was reactionary, confrontational, and overtly threatening. In both cases, the proximity of these groups to the playing surface materially increased the likelihood of a mass incursion and contributed to the rapid escalation of disorder.

"The post-match pitch invasion by several hundred Celtic supporters was wholly inexcusable. It provoked an immediate hostile response from sections of the home support, who forced past stewards and police to reach the pitch."

Mr Blackbourne also noted it is "deeply disturbing" that a post-match Glasgow City Council Special SAG meeting recorded that time-served Police Scotland officers were described as "petrified" of policing another match at Ibrox Stadium.

He added: "That word must be read in context, not in isolation, but so qualified, it remains deeply disturbing for Scottish football.

"This reference demands the most serious attention from all parties with responsibility for the governance of safety and security at major football fixtures in Scotland."

Interviewees independently described the organisational characteristics of certain ultra groups in terms more commonly associated with organised crime groups in the report.

The report called for incidents linked to ultra groups to come down with heavier sanctions from the clubs.

articles.title: Manchester United’s Carrick backs Fernandes and is expected to face Chelsea
articles.summary: Michael Carrick will manage Man Utd at Chelsea on Saturday despite sacking rumours and says Bruno Fernandes will return.
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, under pressure after a woeful run of results, said on Thursday that he was “here to do my job”, insisting he needed “no assurances” over his future at Old Trafford.

Carrick also said he was unsurprised to still be in charge and gave his backing to United captain Bruno Fernandes.

Portugal midfielder Fernandes was left on the bench for last week’s loss at home to Bournemouth following his criticism of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como.

“He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

Carrick’s position has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight football games without a win.

Sunday’s 3-0 humbling loss at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

The 20-time English champions have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Carrick was widely expected to be sacked this week, but he remains in charge after a show of support from the club’s hierarchy.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s match away to Chelsea, the former United and England midfielder was in a defiant mood.

Asked if he was still surprised to be in post, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”

Carrick “doesn’t need assurances” from Manchester United, he said.

Carrick was equally adamant he did not require public backing from the United hierarchy.

“I don’t need assurances from anyone,” he said. “I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that.”

Questioned on Fernandes’s position , Carrick said leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth was a “decision for the game”.

“That’s it. Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I’ve got no issues with that; we move forward. We’re looking forward to the game at the weekend now.”

Carrick appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth.

Moments later, a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch, as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s poor performances.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring a revival as caretaker boss that saw United finish third in the Premier League and return to the Champions League after struggling under manager Ruben Amorim.

But results have been so bad this season that former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford, said on Thursday that “sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good”.

Carrick, however, was adamant he would not walk away from his job, saying: “I’ve said it before, I care about what the supporters think. I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see.

“I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”

This season’s drastic decline is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

But Carrick insisted his much-criticised players felt the sting of poor results every bit as much as the fans.

“The boys are hungry,” he said. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.”

articles.title: Lebrijana - Getafe en directo | Última hora de Copa del Rey en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Balón muy pasado de Valou, imposible para Mayoral. Intenta, con más fe que otra cosa, buscar la acción que le dé el empate la Lebrijana. Revive Yuyo p
articles.body:
Última hora del Lebrijana - Getafe en directo:

Buenas tardes. Bienvenidos a la Copa del Rey. Bienvenidos al Unión Balompédica Lebrijana-Getafe. En menos de dos horas arranca en el Estadio Municipal de Lebrija una de las 56 eliminatorias de esta primera ronda del torneo del KO, marcada, tristemente, por el accidente ferroviario de Urda.

En Lebrija se disputa hoy uno de los duelos a priori más desnivelados de esta ronda. No en vano, se enfrenta un equipo de Primera división con uno de División de Honor Andaluza. Nada menos que cinco categorías de diferencia que veremos si se dejan o no notar cuando el balón eché a rodar.

El Getafe no sólo se juega el pase. También quiere olvidar con una victoria la pesadilla de la pasada semana. Los azulones han visto cómo su equipo ha caído de manera contundente, con nueve goles encajados y una sensación de fragilidad que culminó con las declaraciones de Bordalás señalando que el equipo había "tocado fondo" tras la goleada recibida en San Mamés .

En Copa, Bordalás rotará . De hecho, en rueda de prensa, el alicantino ya dejó entrever que habrá jugadores del filial en la alineación. El cuadro de Manu del Moral nutrirá a un primer equipo que necesita dar descanso a futbolistas con muchos minutos y otros que han podido tener molestias en las últimas semanas.

Con todos estos ingredientes, y con la magia que siempre acompaña a la Copa del Rey , esperamos una noche de emociones en Lebrija . Y aquí estaremos para contarlo.

articles.title: Crystal Palace: Pierre Sage on finding solutions, visiting Roberto De Zerbi and building foundations for future success
articles.summary: Pierre Sage's Crystal Palace earned a much-needed Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday; Frenchman convinced tough start to his reign will help deliver future success; Watch Tottenham Hotspur vs Crystal Palace live on Sky Sports on Saturday from 5pm; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
The Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday night helps. After four games without a win across all competitions, scrutiny was rising. A step into the quarter-finals brought some relief.

A 5-0 hammering at rivals Brighton earlier this month had been a painful low and, after the glory years under Oliver Glasner, the start to the Sage era had alarm bells ringing in some quarters.

But for the Palace head coach, it could be these days which provide the foundation to launch from.

"Maybe you will think my answer is crazy but I think it's an opportunity for me to become a better coach," he told Sky Sports .

"Faced with the difficulty, the problem, you have to find a solution I didn't anticipate. It's an opportunity to challenge my ideas, my way of doing [things], some adaptation...

"I know the most important thing is the results, that we need to change things to become the team we're able to be. I have to take the good decisions at the good moment in this period because the player needs [me to].

"This situation is maybe a positive opportunity for me. Every day I want to improve and become a better coach and help the players and team to become better too."

Sage reckons Palace began to look more like the side he wants them to be in the second half at Craven Cottage. They are small steps but signs of encouragement after a difficult period. He is convinced the work he and his squad are doing behind the scenes is setting them up for positive weeks ahead.

"A lot of time you think you work for nothing but you work always for tomorrow," he said. "You create the roots of something big.

"When you're in this mindset and everyone understands this kind of thing, the pressure is not where everybody thinks - it's on what you do daily."

On Saturday, he takes his Palace side to another team who endured a difficult start to the season but who are also hoping they are experiencing the start of a transformation to their fortunes: Tottenham Hotspur.

Sage is familiar with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi, having travelled to Italy earlier in his career to study his coaching methods.

"He was a model for a long time," said Sage. "I went to Rome, to Sassuolo. I wanted to understand how he plays."

Sage then added with a smile: "All these guys are opponents during two hours but all of them [have] good ideas and I just have to rob them, their good ideas and create a context here to be efficient."

The Frenchman is eager to bring his own distinctive style to south London. "We're not here only to try to win but to win in the way decide. That's really exciting to manage this gap," he said.

Achieving that goal will take time. But Sage - off the back of that Fulham win - is confident it can be achieved with commitment to the process and unity around the club.

"We have to stay calm and confident with what we do and what we have to do," he said.

"The club and the fans have to be together. We're a big family, we love the badge, we fight every day for the badge.

"We are all here for the same things: we want to see this team really competitive on the pitch, win games, win titles and share good moments all together to have things to explain to our family when we will be old."

A win away at Spurs this weekend would be a significant step in the right direction.

articles.title: Colorado's Julian Lewis Recovering After Being Hospitalized for 'Medical Emergency' at Team Facility
articles.summary: Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis is recovering in a hospital after an medical situation at the team's facility on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis is recovering in a hospital after an medical situation at the team's facility on Wednesday.

Lewis' family said in a statement that Julian was transported to a local hospital after experiencing a "medical emergency" and he is in recovery right now.

Colorado's initial injury report this week for Saturday's matchup with Kansas State listed Lewis as doubtful, but there was no official injury designation listed.

Lewis entered this season as the Buffaloes' starting quarterback. He led them to a 2-1 record before being benched at halftime during their Sept. 26 game against Baylor.

Isaac Wilson has started Colorado's last three games and is set to take the reins against Kansas State.

A graduate of Carrollton High School in Carrollton, Georgia, Lewis was a 4-star prospect in the 2025 recruiting class. He committed to Colorado in November 2024.

Lewis made two starts and four appearances during his freshman campaign. He threw for 589 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.

articles.title: France football chief backs Real Madrid’s Mbappe after China apology
articles.summary: Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe should be allowed to move on after apology to China, says French football federation chief.
articles.body:
French Football Federation ‌chief Philippe Diallo said Kylian Mbappe should be allowed to move on ⁠amid controversy over ⁠the France captain referring to former Chinese leader Mao Zedong as a dictator because the player has apologised and intended no offence.

Mbappe’s club ⁠Real Madrid and La Liga have also apologised following the remarks, while the league’s president Javier Tebas set up a crisis unit and met Chinese ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, ⁠on Wednesday as Spanish football sought to contain the fallout .

The backlash highlights the risks for athletes and brands in the lucrative Chinese market, where satire about Mao, modern China’s founding leader who governed the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains ‌a social taboo.

Chinese state media outlet China Daily said Mbappe’s remark had “triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the limits of celebrity influence”.

China’s state-owned broadcaster Migu is not showing Real Madrid’s game at Racing Santander on Sunday, and Chinese brands including dairy companies Mengniu and Shanghai Milkground Food Tech, as well as Eastroc Beverage, have ceased all cooperation with Mbappe .

Diallo expressed hope the issue would soon be ⁠resolved.

“It is a controversy which, ultimately, should not, I hope, last because Kylian has very well explained the context in which this intervention took place. He has apologised,” Diallo was quoted as saying ⁠by French newspaper Ouest-France on Thursday.

“I believe we should now leave it at that so that he can continue his ⁠season in the best possible conditions.”

The controversy stems from ⁠a long-running joke surrounding 27-year-old Mbappe’s influence at club level.

In a video on a French podcast that has since been taken down, Mbappe is heard discussing a meme in which his face had been ‌photoshopped onto that of “some guy”, adding: “I think he’s a Chinese dictator.”

Fans have previously created memes superimposing Mbappe’s face on images of military and political leaders to suggest ‌he ‌has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for. Mbappe has been nicknamed “the dictator” in the European press.

A spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the government is taking Mbappe’s apology “seriously”.

articles.title: Celtic & Rangers Scottish Cup stadium closure upheld
articles.summary: Rangers and Celtic will both play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors after the clubs respective appeals against the sanction was dismissed.
articles.body:
Rangers and Celtic will both play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors after the clubs' respective appeals against the sanction was dismissed.

The Glasgow clubs presented their cases to a Scottish FA appellate tribunal on Monday, but have failed to overturn a ban on supporters.

They will also be required to pay £100,000 to the visiting club in their respective home ties in the national cup competition.

However, a suspended ban on fans in the case of further infractions was set aside by the tribunal.

Celtic criticised , external what they called an "excessive and disproportionate punishment" and claimed a "false equivalence" has been drawn between the behaviour of their own fans entering the pitch "at a moment of emotion and celebration" and that of Rangers supporters.

The club also said it had no responsibility for stadium safety arrangements at Ibrox, and so should not have been punished in the same way as Rangers.

The stadium closure penalty was announced in late August following the disorder at the end of last season's quarter-final tie at Ibrox, which Celtic won after a penalty shoot-out.

Supporters threw fireworks and other missiles and police officers were injured, while 43 arrests had been made by 25 August.

An independent review published in July concluded the incident "came within a very small margin of becoming a violent mass confrontation".

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, identified failings by both clubs and criticised the SFA for not taking a tougher approach to crowd disorder.

An agreement was reached in September to have no away fans at any of the Old Firm derbies in this season's SPFL competitions.

articles.title: England Soccer Player Ivan Toney Pleads Not Guilty to Assault and Trial Set for 2028
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — England striker Ivan Toney appeared in court on Thursday and pleaded not guilty after being accused of headbutting and punching a man at a nightclub in London last year.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — England striker Ivan Toney appeared in court on Thursday and pleaded not guilty after being accused of headbutting and punching a man at a nightclub in London last year.

The 30-year-old Toney, who represented England at the World Cup last summer and plays for Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia, will face a trial in 2028 — during the European Championship soccer tournament being co-hosted by England that year — over the alleged assault.

During the five-minute hearing at Southwark Crown Court in London, Toney formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm following a confrontation at a night spot on Wardour St. on Dec. 6 last year, Britain's Press Association news agency reported.

A provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who apologized to Toney about the delay.

"That's a long way in advance and I'm sorry about that," the judge said. "As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons."

Euro 2028 is scheduled for June 9-July 9 and is being staged in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

Toney was released on unconditional bail, PA news reported.

He started his career with Northampton and played for Newcastle and Peterborough before signing for Brentford in 2020. He joined Al-Ahli in 2024.

Toney has played 10 times for England, scoring once. He wasn't selected in the most recent England squad for Nations League matches in September and October.

articles.title: Ancelotti llama a Vinicius, Endrick y Raphinha, pero deja fuera a Militao
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador de Brasil incluye a los dos atacantes del Real Madrid y al del Barça en su lista para los amistosos de noviembre ante Japón y Singapur
articles.summary: El seleccionador de Brasil incluye a los dos atacantes del Real Madrid y al del Barça en su lista para los amistosos de noviembre ante Japón y Singapur
articles.body: Carlo Ancelotti ha hecho pública la convocatoria de Brasil para el parón de selecciones de noviembre, y en ella figuran dos de los futbolistas del Real Madrid: Vinicius Júnior y Endrick. La gran ausencia madridista es la de Éder Militao, que se queda fuera de la lista pese a haber dejado atrás su lesión. La Canarinha disputará dos amistosos en el Estadio Nacional de Singapur: el 14 de noviembre ante Japón (11:15, hora peninsular española) y el 17 ante Singapur (11:00). El central todavía no entra en los planes del técnico italiano para esta ventana. Militao, que reapareció recientemente con el Madrid tras una larga baja, todavía no ha recuperado el ritmo de competición, y Ancelotti ha preferido no forzar su vuelta a la Canarinha hasta que acumule más minutos. El defensa seguirá, por tanto, cogiendo rodaje con el club durante estas semanas. Tampoco acudirá Rodrygo, como es lógico, ya que se encuentra recuperándose de su larga lesión. Distinto es el caso de los dos atacantes. Endrick, que atraviesa un momento ascendente tras ganarse un hueco en las rotaciones de Mourinho, acude a la llamada de su seleccionador. Y Vinicius también entra en la lista, aunque su situación llega marcada por una particularidad: el brasileño afronta la concentración condicionado por la sanción que cumple en LaLiga. Vinicius arrastra el castigo por el tirón de pelo a Saliba en el partido ante el Villarreal, una acción que le costó la expulsión y cuatro partidos de suspensión en el campeonato doméstico. Ese correctivo no afecta a la competición europea, por lo que el delantero solo disputará con el Madrid, antes del parón, el encuentro de la Liga de Campeones en Atenas, mientras cumple sanción en los compromisos ligueros. La lista incluye también a Raphinha, delantero del Barcelona y uno de los fijos de Ancelotti, cuya convocatoria se sigue con inquietud en el entorno azulgrana. El brasileño arrastra un historial reciente de problemas físicos ligados a la selección: se lesionó en los amistosos de marzo, sufrió una lesión muscular en el Mundial que le apartó de buena parte del torneo y volvió a tener molestias tras el último parón, un goteo que ha obligado al Barça a gestionar en varias ocasiones su recuperación al regreso de las concentraciones.

articles.title: Eagles star emerges as trade candidate ahead of deadline; ‘Rare’ defender could be on move
articles.summary: The Eagles could trade these two players.
articles.body:
The Eagles are a team to watch as the NFL trade deadline approaches — not necessarily for their play on the field but for the moves they make off it.

The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Eagles could make several trades to reload the roster. The Eagles are 2-5, which will make them sellers at the trade deadline.

They could trade impending free agents and older players who don't fit their long-term plans in exchange for draft picks

ESPN ranked 25 trade candidates ahead of the deadline. Two Eagles players made that list, including cornerback Riq Woolen and left guard Landon Dickerson.

"When I talk to rival teams about which players Philly might move, Woolen's name comes up fairly often," ESPN NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler wrote. "He's a high-upside corner and 2027 free agent whose $1.26 million base salary could help facilitate a trade (much of his $12 million in guarantees came via signing or restructured bonuses)."

Woolen has great physical tools, but his inconsistent play during his four years with the Seahawks has cost him money.

He signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this offseason. Woolen has been a favorite of Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio since the spring.

"Well, he's a rare guy in that you don't see many corners in the league that are 6-4...," Fangio said in May. "It's hard to find guys at those heights that can move and mirror receivers that are hard to cover. He can do that for a guy his height. ... He obviously has good downfield speed and his length is more of an asset than a detriment in his case."

Woolen is coming off his worst game of the season. On Monday, he gave up a 16-yard touchdown to Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb and missed a handful of tackles. He allowed big catches on two scoring drives and drew a holding call before Lamb's touchdown.

The Eagles will need him to play better over the next two weeks to boost his trade value.

Fowler gave Woolen a 35% chance of being traded, but had Dickerson at 25%.

"Something feels off between the Eagles and Dickerson, one of the holdovers from the Jeff Stoutland offensive front," Fowler wrote. The Eagles are in a position to recoup draft capital for the future and are going younger on the offensive line. A mix of erratic play and injuries could affect his value, but he has Pro Bowl traits, his guarantees run dry next year, and he held up well in his return for 'Monday Night Football' against the Cowboys."

articles.title: Jack Grealish: England winger dropped by Everton due to 'breach of club discipline'
articles.summary: Jack Grealish is left out of Everton's Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle United on Thursday "due to a breach of club discipline".
articles.body:
Jack Grealish was left out of Everton 's Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle United on Thursday "due to a breach of club discipline". , external

Everton did not disclose any further details but it is believed it was for missing a training session.

England winger Grealish, 31, is on loan at Everton from Premier League rivals Manchester City .
